learner_operation: Translate an already upper-triangular 3x3 system into an augmented matrix, eliminate entries above the third pivot using row 3, then above the second pivot using row 2, and identify the unique RREF or solution among five radio choices.

fixed_features.feature: Nonsingular already-echelon 3x3 system, x/y/z order, easy integer arithmetic
fixed_features.justification: Target title and observed prompts; full-rank unit upper triangular source questions require only backward elimination, not singular cases or forward elimination.

fixed_features.feature: Five-choice radio with matrix, vector or text result
fixed_features.justification: Captured answer-field contract; these three observed representations have the same elimination result.

fixed_features.feature: Unit pivots and two/three active above-pivot entries in random practice
fixed_features.justification: All captured question-bank systems have unit pivots; source q-131586 and q-131588 explicitly skip an already-zero entry. General lesson pivot scaling is a broader demonstrated possibility, not necessary to every easy exercise.

answer_roles.role: Which bank triple solves the displayed system
answer_roles.eligible_variation: All five distinct source-bank candidates can be correct after changing RHS while preserving upper-triangular A.
answer_roles.observed: Controlled tests make each of five roles correct for each of 12 implemented profiles; random delivered and runner batch contain different roles. Missing source replay profiles are recorded separately.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: a12/a13/a23 vary sign and magnitude, including each observed single-zero mask.
answer_roles.observed: Each implemented profile covers all four declared masks, with ±5 boundary coefficients, translations ±5 and scales 1/2. These are justified same-method variations.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Each candidate may occupy any position; no role-position assignment is mathematically necessary.
answer_roles.observed: Raw random arrays have strong late-position bias (40/60 fourth, 19/60 fifth), but actual unmodified UI reorders by hashed item/field/choice IDs. UI fixture samples and five-item batch do not have a fixed correct position; normalization changes IDs and positions again.

coverage.case: Five eligible roles in each implemented source profile
coverage.result: 12 profiles x 5 roles, all four coefficient masks per profile; no bank-geometry predictor answers each role.

coverage.case: Random sampler and exact five-item runner batch before and after filtering
coverage.result: All 60 fresh random items and all 5 runner items survive; decision-case support unchanged. Batch roles 0/1/3 and three masks; no requirement that a five-item batch exhaust every case.

counterfactuals.change: For each response shape hold profile, A, bank, translation, scale and seed fixed; switch correct bank role 0 to 1 and recompute RHS.
counterfactuals.expected: Different displayed RHS and solution; old bank answer rejected and new one accepted; row-operation matrices and final explanations follow displayed equations.
counterfactuals.observed: All three pairs change solution and key correctly, pass independent exact displayed-content checks, native all-choice grading and actual UI rendering.
counterfactuals.justification: RHS values are relevant evidence determining the unique solution; bank role is incidental and eligible to change.

counterfactuals.change: For each shape preserve bank role/solution, negate all active off-diagonal coefficients [2,-3,1] -> [-2,3,-1] and recompute RHS.
counterfactuals.expected: Displayed equations and elimination operations change but final solution value and accepted candidate triple remain the same.
counterfactuals.observed: All three pairs preserve final answer value and native accepted choice, while prompts, intermediate matrices, operation signs and rendered explanations change consistently.
counterfactuals.justification: The particular upper-triangular representation of the same solution is irrelevant to which triple is correct; operations themselves must track changed coefficients. UUID identities and visible order may change.

shortcut_probes.cue: one choice agrees with directly given z
shortcut_probes.subgroup: runner batch with unique matching z
shortcut_probes.strategy: Read z from final equation and choose sole matching third coordinate
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Blind baseline 0.2. This works on 2 of 5 batch items; three remaining items need more coordinates. Directly reading the last pivot equation is mathematical reasoning expressly present in every source system, and justified simplifications are allowed. No label/layout-only strategy demonstrated.

limitations: Missing source replays q-20598, q-20589 and e-4709 require revision independently of these supported-family variation checks.
